clips.send: An entrepreneur sends this to a cautious friend: the awe that a total stranger risked everything on one idea.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says a stranger at a New York deli heard about his memory course and said, "I'll put up all the money." No resume, no pitch deck - just a man who recognized value and moved before he could talk himself out of it.

That is the real lesson behind every big break: the people who get rich are not smarter. They say yes faster than everyone else says no.

clips.send: A job seeker sends this to a friend before an interview: the anxiety of being overlooked, and proof memory alone can beat 100 rivals.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says one of his memory course students called into a radio show and told this story: he had memorized all 1,500 New York Stock Exchange ticker symbols before a job interview against over 100 other applicants.

He got the job. Then three promotions. His own words after: "Everybody thinks I am smart. I am not sure if I am - I just appear to be a genius."
